headline: 64 goals in 56 games: Haaland leads Norway to victory over Denmark
summary: The Manchester City star scored twice in a 3-2 win, further extending his record as the Nations League's all-time top scorer.
details: Erling Haaland continued his prolific scoring form, netting twice as Norway defeated Denmark 3-2 in a thrilling Nations League opener in Oslo.
The result takes Haaland's international tally to 64 goals in just 56 appearances, maintaining an extraordinary scoring rate for his country.
Norway took an early lead through Oscar Bobb, before Haaland added a second. Denmark fought back to level the game through Mikkel Damsgaard and Rasmus Hojlund.
In the 74th minute, Haaland secured the win with a powerful finish from a well-worked corner, marking his second goal of the night.
Haaland has now scored in 15 of his last 16 competitive games for Norway, totaling 29 goals during that specific span.
With 21 Nations League goals, the striker now sits atop the all-time scoring chart for the competition, leading Cristiano Ronaldo and Aleksandar Mitrović.
The Norwegian forward has also managed multiple goals in eight of his last 10 competitive international appearances.
caption:
64 goals in 56 games. Erling Haaland simply refuses to stop scoring.

Erling Haaland continued his prolific scoring form, netting twice as Norway defeated Denmark 3-2 in a thrilling Nations League opener in Oslo.

The result takes Haaland's international tally to 64 goals in just 56 appearances, maintaining an extraordinary scoring rate for his country.

Norway took an early lead through Oscar Bobb, before Haaland added a second. Denmark fought back to level the game through Mikkel Damsgaard and Rasmus Hojlund.

In the 74th minute, Haaland secured the win with a powerful finish from a well-worked corner, marking his second goal of the night.

Haaland has now scored in 15 of his last 16 competitive games for Norway, totaling 29 goals during that specific span.

With 21 Nations League goals, the striker now sits atop the all-time scoring chart for the competition, leading Cristiano Ronaldo and Aleksandar Mitrović.

The Norwegian forward has also managed multiple goals in eight of his last 10 competitive international appearances.

headline: Local government polls likely in January
summary: The Election Commission has deferred the tentative timeline for local polls due to student examinations in November and December.
details: The Election Commission (EC) has indicated that local government elections, including Union Parishad polls, will likely be held in January.
Election Commissioner Anwarul Islam Sarkar stated that the tentative timeline was delayed because of students' annual examinations scheduled for November and December.
Sarkar explained that holding polls during the examination period would be difficult as law enforcement agencies would be occupied with security at examination centres.
The commission is considering announcing the schedule 40 to 45 days before the voting date in January.
Previously, the EC had announced November 12 as a tentative date for the first phase of UP elections across 80 upazilas, but this was later deferred.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam had previously noted that the EC announced those dates without consulting the government.
The EC has denied that government pressure led to the delay, attributing it solely to practical considerations and the academic calendar.
caption:
Local government elections are now expected in January. The Election Commission has pushed back the dates to avoid clashing with student exams.

The Election Commission (EC) has indicated that local government elections, including Union Parishad polls, will likely be held in January.

Election Commissioner Anwarul Islam Sarkar stated that the tentative timeline was delayed because of students' annual examinations scheduled for November and December.

Sarkar explained that holding polls during the examination period would be difficult as law enforcement agencies would be occupied with security at examination centres.

The commission is considering announcing the schedule 40 to 45 days before the voting date in January.

Previously, the EC had announced November 12 as a tentative date for the first phase of UP elections across 80 upazilas, but this was later deferred.

State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam had previously noted that the EC announced those dates without consulting the government.

The EC has denied that government pressure led to the delay, attributing it solely to practical considerations and the academic calendar.
